pages.title: The Elements of Programming: Expressions & Values
bulletPoints: Lisp / Scheme computational model: Prefix notation (+ 1 2) providing uniform syntax for all operator applications.
Evaluating combinations: Evaluate sub-expressions, then apply operator procedure to argument values.
Naming and the Environment: (define size 2) binding symbolic names to computational values.
Special forms: Expressions with custom evaluation rules (define, if, cond, lambda) that bypass standard applicative order.

pages.title: Procedures and the Processes They Generate
bulletPoints: Linear Recursive processes: Expanding chain of deferred operations consuming stack space O(n).
Linear Iterative processes: State captured entirely in state variables; executed in constant memory space O(1).
Tail-Call Optimization (TCO): Scheme guarantee that iterative algorithms described recursively run in constant stack space.
Case study: Comparing recursive factorial with tail-recursive accumulator factorial.

pages.title: Higher-Order Procedures & Abstractions
bulletPoints: Procedures as First-Class Citizens: Procedures can be passed as arguments, returned as values, and stored in data structures.
Abstracting common patterns: Summation procedure taking term and next functions to compute arbitrary mathematical series.
Lambda expressions: Constructing anonymous procedures on the fly via (lambda (x) (* x x)).
Let bindings: Syntactic sugar for anonymous lambda applications creating localized lexical scopes.

pages.title: Procedures as General Methods
bulletPoints: Finding roots of equations by half-interval method (bisection algorithm over continuous functions).
Fixed points of functions: Computing f(x) = x through repeated iteration with average damping.
Newton's Method for square roots expressed as a general fixed-point transformation.
Procedures as returned values: Higher-order procedures returning derivative approximations and function transforms.

pages.title: Data Abstraction: Building with Pairs
bulletPoints: Compound data: Combining data objects to form structured computational representations.
Pairs: The fundamental primitive (cons x y), with selectors (car p) for first element and (cdr p) for second element.
Closure property of data: The ability to combine pairs whose elements are themselves pairs, building hierarchical structures.
Data abstraction barrier: Using constructor make-rat and selectors numer/denom to decouple representations from operations.

pages.title: Hierarchical Data & The List Structure
bulletPoints: List representation: Chains of pairs terminated by empty list '() / nil.
List operations: (length lst), (append list1 list2), and recursive list reversal.
Mapping over lists: The higher-order (map proc lst) transforming every element in a list.
Trees: Modeling nested lists as tree branches; counting leaves and mapping over tree nodes.

pages.title: Sequences as Conventional Interfaces
bulletPoints: Signal-flow architecture: Enumerating, filtering, mapping, and accumulating data streams.
Filter, Accumulate (fold-right), and Flatmap operations on list sequences.
Nested mappings: Solving the prime-sum-pairs problem using sequence comprehension idioms.
Eight-Queens Puzzle: Solving constraint satisfaction problems through sequence transformations.

pages.title: Symbolic Data & Symbolic Differentiation
bulletPoints: Quotation: Preventing evaluation using 'symbol to manipulate literal language symbols as data.
Symbolic algebra: Representing algebraic expressions (+ x 3) as nested Scheme lists.
Differentiation rules: Implementing the derivative operator d/dx for sums, products, and powers.
Simplification: Algebraic canonical reduction (e.g. (+ x 0) -> x, (* x 1) -> x) through constructor pattern matching.

pages.title: Multiple Representations for Abstract Data
bulletPoints: Complex numbers: Rectangular coordinates (real, imag) vs Polar coordinates (magnitude, angle).
Type tagging: Attaching type tags ('rectangular, 'polar) to data objects to guide runtime dispatch.
Data-directed programming: Organizing operations and types in a two-dimensional dispatch table.
Message-passing style: Objects represented as procedures that dispatch on incoming method messages.

pages.title: Generic Arithmetic Operations
bulletPoints: Designing a generic arithmetic system supporting ordinary numbers, rational numbers, and complex numbers.
Two-dimensional coercion table: Coercing types into common super-types (e.g. integer -> real -> complex).
Tower of types: Hierarchical subtyping and automatic raising of arguments in arithmetic expressions.
Symbolic polynomials: Extending generic arithmetic to handle multi-variable polynomial algebra.

pages.title: Modularity, Objects & State
bulletPoints: Assignment operator (set! var val): Introducing mutable state into functional programming.
The cost of assignment: Loss of the Substitution Model of evaluation; referential transparency is broken.
Local state variables: Encapsulating private state variables inside closure procedures (e.g. bank account balance).
Sameness vs change: The philosophical challenge of identity when objects mutate over time.

pages.title: The Environment Model of Evaluation
bulletPoints: Frames and Environments: An environment is a chain of frames; each frame is a table of variable-value bindings.
Evaluating a lambda expression: Creates a procedure object containing procedure code and a pointer to the enclosing environment.
Applying a procedure: Creates a new frame whose enclosing environment is the procedure's creation environment.
Tracing local state: How closures maintain persistent state across function invocations.

pages.title: Mutable Data Structures & Queues
bulletPoints: Mutating pairs: Primitive mutators (set-car! pair val) and (set-cdr! pair val).
Queue implementation: Maintaining front-pointer and rear-pointer in a pair for O(1) insertion and deletion.
Tables / Dictionaries: 1D and 2D associative tables constructed from key-value pair chains.
Circuit simulator: Event-driven simulation modeling logic gates, wires, and propagation delays with agenda queues.

pages.title: Concurrency: Time and Mutable State
bulletPoints: The nature of time in programs with state: Interleaved concurrent execution producing race conditions.
Bank account transfer bug: Interleaving balance checks and withdrawals across concurrent threads.
Serializers: Mutex synchronization ensuring only one thread executes a critical section at any instant.
Deadlock in concurrent programs: Two threads acquiring serializers in opposite orders.

pages.title: Streams: Delayed Evaluation & Lazy Lists
bulletPoints: The dilemma of lists: Processing large sequences forces all intermediate elements into memory simultaneously.
Stream abstraction: Streams are lazy lists where elements are constructed only on demand (memoized delay).
Primitives: (cons-stream a b) expands into (cons a (delay b)); (stream-car s) and (stream-cdr s) forces evaluation.
Infinite streams: Representing the infinite stream of integers, Fibonacci numbers, and prime numbers in constant memory.

pages.title: Stream Processing & Signal Processing
bulletPoints: Implicit stream definitions: (define ones (cons-stream 1 ones)) and stream addition.
Sieve of Eratosthenes: Elegant prime generation filtering infinite integer streams.
Series approximations: Computing pi and e through Euler's accelerated stream transformations.
Modeling systems with state: Replacing mutable state variables with stateless infinite streams of successive states.

pages.title: The Metacircular Evaluator: Core Architecture
bulletPoints: Metacircular Evaluator: An interpreter written in the same language it is interpreting (eval and apply cycle).
The Eval function: Classifying expressions (self-evaluating, variables, quotes, assignments, definitions, conditionals, lambdas).
The Apply function: Unpacking primitive procedures vs compound procedures and binding arguments in new environment frames.
The eval-apply mutually recursive engine driving computational execution.

pages.title: Representing Expressions & Data Structures
bulletPoints: Syntactic abstractions: Separating syntax representation from evaluator implementation.
Tagged lists: Testing (pair? exp) and (eq? (car exp) 'if) to identify expression forms.
Representing environments: Association lists of variable-value pairs and enclosing parent environment pointers.
Error handling and driver loop: Reading expressions from prompt, evaluating, and printing results (REPL).

pages.title: Evaluator Data as Programs
bulletPoints: Syntactic analysis separation: Analyzing expressions once to produce execution procedures, accelerating interpretation.
Separating analysis from execution: Pre-compiling AST expressions into closures accepting only an environment parameter.
Performance optimization: Eliminating repeated syntax parsing inside high-iteration loops.
Homoiconicity: Code is data; programs can generate, analyze, and execute new programs seamlessly.

pages.title: Variations on a Scheme: Lazy Evaluation
bulletPoints: Normal-order evaluation: Delaying argument evaluation until their values are strictly required by primitive procedures.
Thunks: Wrapping unevaluated arguments in environments and memoizing results upon first evaluation.
Lazy Scheme interpreter: Modifying eval and apply to support non-strict procedure parameters.
Infinite data structures as first-class objects: Passing infinite lists directly to ordinary procedures.

pages.title: Nondeterministic Computing: The Amb Evaluator
bulletPoints: Nondeterministic choice: (amb e1 e2 ... en) returns one of the values, backtracking if subsequent code fails.
The (require p) primitive: Prunes search branches where predicate p is false, triggering automatic backtracking.
Automatic search: Solving logic puzzles (e.g. Liars puzzle, Multiple dwelling puzzle) through nondeterministic choice.
Continuation-passing implementation: Success continuations and failure continuations managing backtracking execution paths.

pages.title: Logic Programming & The Query System
bulletPoints: Declarative programming: Expressing WHAT is true rather than HOW to calculate it.
Deductive information retrieval: Querying databases of assertions and relational rules.
Pattern matching: Comparing query patterns against database assertions containing variable tokens ?x.
Unification: Generalization of pattern matching finding variable substitutions that make two symbolic expressions identical.

pages.title: Register Machines & Hardware Models
bulletPoints: Register Machine model: Data paths (registers, ALU operations) controlled by a finite state Controller.
Designing instruction sequences for GCD (Greatest Common Divisor) and iterative factorial machines.
Subroutines and stacks: Adding a LIFO stack to execute recursive procedures (recursive factorial and Fibonacci).
Simulating register machines in Scheme: Building a software simulator executing register machine assembly instructions.

pages.title: Compilation to Register Machines
bulletPoints: Compiler vs Interpreter: Compiling source Scheme expressions directly into native register machine instructions.
Code generation targets: Preserving registers across sub-expression evaluations.
Compiling expressions: Linkages (return, next, or branch targets) and register allocation strategy.
Combining compiled code and interpreted code: Interfacing compiled routines with the metacircular evaluator.

pages.title: Epilogue: Computing as Pure Thought
bulletPoints: The deep unity of computer science: Procedures as data, data as procedures, and the universal evaluator.
Abstraction as intellectual lever: Managing complexity by constructing layers of expressive languages.
Turing completeness and Church-Turing thesis: The equivalence of Scheme, lambda calculus, and Turing machines.
The wizard book legacy: Programming as an expressive artistic medium for human understanding.
